answer: Before a lab may bill a test, the CLIA registry binds one certificate number to one street address, one lab director and one proficiency testing enrollment, so a second bench reusing it is refused at intake. A duplicate number in the testing feed trips revocation, a civil money penalty and a Medicare payment suspension. A high complexity certificate runs 1800, enrollment 600 and inspection travel 400, so N fakes burn N x 2800 plus N credentialed directors and N years of results. A fable on the website, an atlas in the lobby and a mirror in the draw change nothing in that registry.
